questions.question: Tea and Coffee are grown in _______ soil.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Laterite**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Laterite soils are very suitable for tea, espresso and cashew cultivation.
 
• **Laterite soils lack fertility due to intensive leaching.**
 
• When manured and irrigated, some Laterite are fantastic for developing the plantation floras like tea,coffee, rubber, cinchona, coconut, areca nut, etc,
 
• **Tea and coffee crops demand evenly distributed rainfall and no problems of water logging.**
 
• The hill slopes provide an easy drainage for rain water and helps to prevent water logging. 
 
• The** tea and coffee plantations grow well in loamy soil that is found in large quantities on the hill slopes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alluvial Soil:**

 
 
• It is widespread in the northern plains and river valleys.
 
• It covers about 40% of the total land area of the country.
 
 
 
• **Black Soil:**
 
 
• It is also known as **'Regur Soil**' or the Black cotton Soil.
 
• It covers most of the Deccan Plateau.
 
 
 
• **Arid Soil:**
 
 
• It is also known as desert soil.
 
• It is primarily found in the parts of Haryana, Western Rajasthan, and Punjab, and elongates up to the Rann of Kutch in Gujarat.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT a feature of 'soil'?

options.text: It is made up of inorganic matter.
It covers the surface of the earth.
It is a thin layer of grainy substance.
It is made up of minerals.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__ **It is made up of inorganic matter.**____** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Soil

 
 
• Soil is a combination of organic matter, gases, liquids, and organisms that support life.
 
• Soil is a living natural element.
 
• It is made up of both mineral and organic material.
 
• Soil properties are determined by the parent rock.
 
• Most soils have a dry bulk density of 1.1 to 1.6 g/cm3.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• There is **8 main Type soil **:

 

 
• **Alluvial Soil:**

 
 
• Found in the river plains and deltas of the Ganges, Brahmaputra, and Indus.
 
• Rich in potash but deficient in phosphorus.
 
• Suitable for crops like wheat, rice, sugarcane, and cotton.
 
 
 
• **Black Soil:**
 
 
• Also known as Regur soil, found in the Deccan Plateau (Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu).
 
• Rich in lime, iron, magnesium, and alumina; retains moisture.
 
• Suitable for cotton, known as "Black Cotton Soil."
 
 
 
• **Red and Yellow Soil:**
 
 
• Found in the Eastern and Southern parts of the Deccan Plateau (Odisha, Chhattisgarh, southern parts of the Middle Ganga plain, and along the piedmont zone of the Western Ghats).
 
• Rich in iron but poor in nitrogen, phosphorus, and humus.
 
• Suitable for crops like rice, ragi, tobacco, and vegetables.
 
 
 
• **Laterite Soil:**
 
 
• Found in areas with high rainfall (Western Ghats, Eastern Ghats, parts of Odisha, and Meghalaya).
 
• Rich in iron and aluminum but poor in nitrogen, potassium, and organic matter.
 
• Suitable for crops like tea, coffee, cashew nuts, and tapioca.
 
 
 
• **Arid and Desert Soil:**
 
 
• Found in the arid regions of Rajasthan, Gujarat, and the northern parts of Karnataka.
 
• Sandy and saline, low in organic matter and moisture content.
 
• Suitable for drought-resistant crops like bajra, jowar, and pulses.
 
 
 
• **Saline and Alkaline Soil:**
 
 
• Found in arid and semi-arid regions of Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh.
 
• Contains high amounts of sodium, potassium, and magnesium salts.
 
• Requires soil treatment for cultivation; suitable for salt-tolerant crops like barley, cotton, and sugar beet.
 
 
 
• **Peaty and Marshy Soil:**
 
 
• Found in areas with heavy rainfall and high humidity, such as Kerala, coastal areas of Odisha, and West Bengal.
 
• Rich in organic matter but deficient in potash and phosphate.
 
• Suitable for rice and jute cultivation.
 
 
 
• **Forest and Mountain Soil:**
 
 
• Found in the Himalayan region, Western and Eastern Ghats, and some parts of the peninsular plateau.
 
• Rich in humus but poor in potash, phosphorus, and lime.
 
• Suitable for tea, coffee, spices, and temperate fruits.

questions.question: Which type of soil retains the maximum amount of water?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Clay.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Clayey soil **retains the highest amount of water and sandy soil retains the lowest amount of water.
 
• Clay soil is soil that is comprised of very fine mineral particles and not much organic material. 
 
• Clay is the smallest particle among the other two types of soil.
 
• The particles in this soil are tightly packed together with each other with very little or no airspace.
 
• This soil has very good water storage qualities and makes it hard for moisture and air to penetrate into it.
 
 
• It is very sticky to the touch when wet, but smooth when dried. 
 
 
 
• Clay is the densest and heaviest type of soil that does not drain well or provide space for plant roots to flourish.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sand **is a granular material composed of finely divided rock and mineral particles.

 
 
• Sand has various compositions but is defined by its grain size. 
 
 
 
• **Silt **is granular material of a size between sand and clay and composed mostly of broken grains of quartz.
 
 
• Silt may occur as soil or as sediment mixed in suspension with water. 
 
 
 
• **Loam **is soil composed mostly of sand, silt, and a smaller amount of clay.
 
 
• By weight, its mineral composition is about 40–40–20% concentration of sand–silt–clay.

questions.question: Which of the following crops is NOT suitable to be grown in laterite soils?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jute**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jute** may be grown in a variety of soils, from clay to sandy loam, although it thrives on loamy **alluvial soils**.
 
• This crop does not grow well on laterite or gravel soils. The finest soils for jute production are fresh grey alluvial soils with good depth and silt from annual floods.
 
• **Laterite soil **may be found at the eastern margin of the plateau, encompassing tiny areas of Tamil Nadu, Odisha, and a small portion of Chotanagpur in the north, as well as Meghalaya in the north-east.
 
• Although it is unfavourable for agriculture, it is used to** cultivate coffee, rubber, cinchona, cashew, coconut, and other crops**.
 
• The weathering of laterite rocks produced by high temperatures and heavy rains with alternate dry and wet spells results in the formation of this soil.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Laterite** is rich in iron and aluminium soil and rock type that is thought to have originated in hot, humid tropical climates.
 
• Because of the high iron oxide concentration, nearly all laterites are rusty-red in colour.

questions.question: The process of growing different crops successively on the same plot to improve soil health is called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Crop Rotation.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Crop rotation:**

 
 
• **​**It is the practice of growing a series of different types of crops in the same area across a sequence of growing seasons.
 
• It reduces reliance on one set of nutrients, pest and weed pressure, and the probability of developing resistant pests and weeds.​
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Sequential Farming**

 
 
• ​Growing two or more crops in sequence on the same field per year is known as Sequential Farming.
 
• The succeeding crop is planted after the preceding crop has been harvested.
 
• Example- 
 
 
• **Planting maize in the long rains, then beans during the short rains. **
 
 
 
• Management of water and nutrients is modified by the effect of the preceding crop on the succeeding crop.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a method of soil conservation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Overgrazing.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

Some other methods of soil conservation are:

 
• Mulching:

 
 
• A covering of organic materials, such as straw, is applied to the bare ground between plants.
 
• It helps to retain soil moisture.
 
 
 
• Rock dam:
 
 
• Rocks are piled up to slow the flow of water.
 
• This prevents gullies and further soil loss.
 
 
 
• Contour barriers:
 
 
• Along contours, stones, grass, and soil are used to create barriers.
 
• To collect water, trenches are dug in front of the barriers.
 
 
 
• Intercropping:
 
 
• Various crops are cultivated in alternate rows and sowed at different times to protect the soil from rainwash.
 
 
 
• Contour ploughing:
 
 
• Ploughing parallel to the contours of a hill slope creates a natural barrier for water to flow down the slope.
 
 
 
• Shelterbelts:
 
 
• Rows of trees are planted in coastal and dry regions to reduce wind movement and protect soil cover.
 
 
 
• Terrace farming is a method of soil conservation.
 
 
• It is a method of soil conservation that is practised on hilly terrain.
 
• On steep slopes of a hill, broad flat steps or terraces are built so that level surfaces can be used to cultivate crops.
 
• They reduce surface runoff and soil erosion. 
 
 
 
• **Hence overgrazing is not the method to conserve soil.**

questions.question: The entire northern plains of India are made of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Alluvial soil.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Alluvial soil is the most widely spread and important soil,** the entire northern plains are made of alluvial soil**.
 
• These have been deposited by three important **Himalayan river systems**- the Indus, the Ganga, and the Brahmaputra.
 
• They are mainly derived from the debris brought down from the Himalayas or the silt left out by the retreating sea. Thus, they are azonal soils.
 
• Alluvial soils are widespread in the northern plains and the river valleys.
 
• Through a narrow corridor in Rajasthan, they extend into the plains of Gujarat. In the Peninsular region, they are found in deltas of the east coast and in the river valleys.
 
• Alluvial soil is considered the most fertile soil and the entire northern plains of India are made of alluvial soil.
 
• This soil contains sand, silt, and clay.
 
• According to age, the alluvial soil is mainly classified as** Bangar (old alluvial) and Khadar (new alluvial).**
 
• This soil contains an ample amount of potash, phosphoric acid, and lime.
 
• **Suitable Crops:** Wheat, rice, maize, sugarcane, pulses, oilseeds, fruits and vegetables, and leguminous crops.

questions.question: Which of the following factors is NOT responsible for the loss of fertility of agricultural land?

options.text: Higher cation exchange capacity of soil

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Higher cation exchange capacity of soil.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Soil fertility** decline occurs when the quantities of nutrients removed from the soil in harvested products exceed the quantities of nutrients being applied.
 
• The nutrient requirements of the crop are met from soil reserves until these reserves cannot meet crop demands.
 
• This results in a reduction of plant growth and yield.
 
• **Nutrients may be removed from the soil by:**
 
 
• Growing extensive crops
 
• Soil erosion
 
• Leaching.
 
• Alkalisation of soil
 
• Salinisation of soil
 
• Waterlogging
 
 
 
• **Higher cation exchange **usually indicates more clay and organic matter is present in the soil, high CEC soils generally have greater water holding capacity than low CEC soils.
 
• **Hence Higher cation exchange capacity of soil is NOT responsible for the loss of fertility of agricultural land.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Fertility can be maintained with the maintenance** of soil organic matter, soil structure, soil nutrient status and satisfactory soil pH.**
 
• This can be achieved in cropping systems by:
 
 
• including pasture phases and leguminous crops
 
• including the addition of soil amendments or fertilisers
 
• employing a reduced tillage system
 
• retaining crop residues on site.

questions.question: Which part of the soil contains humus?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A-horizon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****A. Horizon or Surface soil** 

__
 
• It is the part of the topsoil.
 
• In this layer, organic matter is mixed with mineral matter.
 
• It is the layer of mineral soil with the most organic matter accumulation and soil life.
 
• Nutrients like iron, aluminium, clay, and organic matter are sometimes dissolved and carried out in this layer.
 
• This layer is depleted of (eluviated of) iron, clay, aluminium, organic compounds, and other soluble constituents.
 
• When depletion is pronounced, a lighter-coloured “E” subsurface soil horizon is apparent at the base of the “A” horizon.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Soil Profile: 

 
• It is the vertical section of soil from all its horizons. 
 
• There are different types of soil, each with its own set of characteristics.
 
• It is made of layers, or horizons (O, A, E, B, C, R). 
 
• Put the horizons together, and they form a soil profile.
 
• Most soil profiles cover the earth as 2 main layers Topsoil and Subsoil.
 
• Most soils have three major horizons (A, B, C) and some have an organic horizon (O).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0ac5af8f6ec28d31d53a9d31b84cc424c86676e70e20fae8e0fd0a9063c47552.png] ​

__
 
• **Alluvial soil is not found In the Himalayan region.**
 
• **Alluvial soils:**
 
 
• These soils are called** transported soil** because although they are formed near the water bodies, these soils get transported from their origin to several other places by various natural agents, especially by gravity.

• The** main crops **cultivated are wheat, rice, maize, sugarcane, pulses, and oilseeds.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• On the basis of **genesis, color, composition, and location,** the soils of India have been classified into:

 
 
• (1) Alluvial soils (ii) Black soils (iii) Red and Yellow soils (iv) Laterite soils (V) Arid soils (vi) Saline soils (vii) Peaty soils (viii) Forest soils.
 
 
 
• On the** basis of the size of the particles **that make up a soil defines its gardening characteristics:
 
 
• (1) Clay soil (ii) Silty soil (iii) Sandy soil (iv) Stones (v) Chalky soils
 
 
 
• **Saline soil:**
 
 
• It refers to Arid soil.
 
• These are derived from the disintegration of adjacent rocks and are largely blown from coastal regions and the Indus valley.
 
• They are developed in western Rajasthan. Due to the dry climate, high temperature and accelerated evaporation, they lack moisture and humus.
 
 
 
• **Calcerous soil:**
 
 
• They are also known as chalky soils.
 
• These soils contain calcium carbonate or lime.
 
• They are very alkaline and may be light or heavy.

questions.question: ______ is the integrated approach to study soil as a collection of natural bodies.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pedology.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pedology** is the integrated approach to study soil as a collection of natural bodies.
 
• The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) has classified soils into **8 categories.**
 
• **Alluvial Soil, Black Cotton Soil or Regur Soil, Red Soil, Laterite Soil, Mountainous or Forest Soils, Arid or Desert Soil, Saline and Alkaline Soil, Peaty and Marshy Soil.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__**Ecology**__

__
 
• **Ecology **is the branch of science that deals with the relationships between living organisms, including humans, and their physical environment.
 
• An ecosystem consists of a community of organisms together with their physical environment consists of two components Biotic and Abiotic.
 
 
• **Biotic **consists of living organisms **(Producers, Consumers, Decomposers).**
 
• **Abiotic** consists of non-living organisms **(air, water, soil, and Sunlight).**
 
 
 
• The food chain is a linear sequence of organisms where nutrients and energy transferred from one organism to another.
 
 
• **Producers__** make their own food Producers include all autotrophs such as plants. They are called **autotrophs** as they can produce food through the process of **photosynthesis.**
 
• **__Primary Consumers__** depend on the producers. Example - Rat.
 
• **__Secondary consumers__** depend on the primary consumer for energy. Example- Snake.
 
• **__Tertiary consumers__** depend on the secondary consumers for the food. Example- Eagle.
 
• **__Decomposers __**are microorganisms that decompose the dead and decaying material into humus which enriches the soil. Example - Bacteria, Fungus.
 
 

__**Serology**__

__
 
• Serology is the study of **antibodies in blood serum.**
 
• **Blood **is a fluid connective tissue and composed of plasma, **blood corpuscles, and platelets.**
 
• It is slightly **basic** in nature **(pH value is between 7.35-7.45)**.
 
• Blood is the constituent of 7% body weight usually in male, the total volume of blood is **5-6 liters** and in female is **4-5 liters**.
 
• The **oxygenated blood** is **bright red** while the** deoxygenated blood** is** purple** in colour.
 
 
• **Plasma**__: is a straw viscous fluid and consists of 92% of water and 8% of proteins **(Fibrinogen, Albumin, Globulin).**
 
• __**Red Blood Corpuscles**__: RBC is also known as** Erythrocytes** and produced in the **bone marrow**. RBC is stored in the** spleen**. RBC is destroyed in the **liver**. The lifespan of RBC is **120 days**. **Haemoglobin** is responsible for the **red colour of the blood**. The amount of haemoglobin in male is **14-15%** while in female is **13-14%.**
 
• __**White Blood Corpuscles**__: WBC is also known as **Leukocytes** and produced in the** bone marrow**. WBC protects our **immune system**. WBC is destroyed in the** liver**. The lifespan of WBC is **2-3 weeks**.
 
• __**Platelets**__: contains the clotting factors and produced in the bone marrow. Platelet is destroyed in the spleen. The lifespan of a platelet is 5-9 days.
 
 

__**Oenology**__

__
 
• Oenology is the science and **study of wine and winemaking.​**

questions.question: Which of the following type of soils in India is locally known as ‘Regur soil’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Black cotton soil**__.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• Black cotton soils are **defunct clays of medium to high compressibility** and form a vital soil group in India.
 
• They are categorized by **high shrinkage and swelling properties**.
 
• This Black cotton soils grows generally in the **central and western parts** and covers approximately 20% of the total area of India.
 
• Because of its** highly bump, inflammation and shrinkage characteristics**, the** Black cotton soils (BC soils**) has been a defiance to highway engineers.
 
• The Black cotton soils are very arduous when dry, but **loses their strength totally when in wet condition**.

questions.question: The pH of soil can be raised by adding ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**limestone**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Limestone** is usually **added to acid soils to increase soil pH**.
 
• The addition of lime not only **replaces hydrogen ions and raises soil pH**, thereby eliminating most major problems associated with acid soils but it also **provides two nutrients, calcium,** and** magnesium to the soil**.
 
• **Inherent factors** that affect soil pH include **climate, mineral content, **and** soil texture**.
 
• Natural soil pH reflects the combined effects of the soil-forming factors **(parent material, time, relief or topography, climate, and organisms)**.
 
• The pH of newly formed soils is determined by the minerals in the parent material.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Some common liming materials are
 
 
• **Calcic limestone is ground limestone.**
 
• **Dolomitic limestone** from **ground limestone high in magnesium.**
 
• Miscellaneous sources such as** wood ashes.**

questions.question: The bare ground between plants is covered with a layer of organic matter like straw. It helps to retain soil moisture. Identify the process.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mulching**__**.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mulching** is a practice of covering the topsoil surface with organic materials like straw, grass, stones inorganic materials like plastics, etc.
 
• **Contour barriers** are contour strips that intercept downslope flowing water and soil particles. These barriers slow down the water movement and reduce its erosive force.
 
• **Contour ploughing** or contour farming is the farming practice of ploughing and/or planting across a slope following its elevation contour lines. These contour lines create a water break which reduces the formation of rills and gullies during times of heavy water run-off; which is a major cause of soil erosion.
 
• **Soil mixing** consists of using specially designed augers or special tools to mechanically mix the soil with in situ binders. The process simultaneously breaks up the soil without removing it.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 
 
Mulching

 
 
 
Layer applied to soil to conserve its moisture and fertility

 
 
 

 
 
Contour barriers

 
 
 
Strips built on slopes to reduce the speed of water for conservation purposes

 
 
 

 
 
Terrace farming

 
 
 
Farming done of slopes in the form of terraces to utilise land effectively
